analysis: The PR changes only docs/developer/test.md: it bumps the Last updated date (line 3) and adds a documentation paragraph at head lines ~541-566 for an opt-in live test, ModelCheckpointConversationLiveTests. The test is not itself in the supplied evidence. The text describes a six-turn growing-conversation observation using an isolated ephemeral cache. It requires native live and checkpoint precision, refuses MiMo, reads only model, precision and outputTokens from the spec, and writes a report to a caller-supplied new path. The documented command uses `env -i` with a minimal environment and `--skip-build`. It adds the env var DARKBLOOM_CHECKPOINT_CONVERSATION_STAGE_MB, which maps to DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB. No runtime code, authorization, attestation, encryption or billing behavior changes. Relevant threats are T-041 (prefix cache, TB-007) and A-001. The documented test uses an isolated ephemeral cache and does not weaken the production gate, TTL, HMAC naming or purge points. The report records only TTFT, restored-token counts and file/byte counts, not prompt content. Remaining questions for later review: the actual test source and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_MAX_STAGE_MB handling were not supplied. If they ship in the same change, confirm they cannot leak a persistent cache key, use production roots, or write reports to unsafe paths. A documentation-only change gives no evidence of a security regression.
